question: If the first quartile of data set 8, 10, 8, 7, 9 is 7.5, then the value of quartile deviation is
solution:
The correct answer is **1.0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **quartile deviation**, also known as semi-interquartile range (IQR), is a measure of dispersion in a data set and is calculated as the difference between the third quartile (Q3) and the first quartile (Q1).

 
 
• It is a robust statistic, meaning it is not affected by outliers in the data set as much as the range or standard deviation.
 
• It is a useful summary statistic when comparing the spread of data sets with different sample sizes, as it is not influenced by sample size in the same way that the standard deviation is.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Given the first quartile of the data set is 7.5, we can calculate the IQR as follows:
 
 
• IQR = Q3 - Q1 Since the data set has 5 observations, Q3 can be calculated as the median of the upper half of the data set, which is (9 + 10) / 2 = 9.5. Therefore, IQR = 9.5 - 7.5 = 2.0
 
• Finally, the quartile deviation can be calculated as IQR / 2 = 2.0 / 2 = 1.0
 
 
• So, the value of quartile deviation is 1.0.
 
 
 
 
 
• The **quartile deviation** (also known as semi-interquartile range) is a measure of the dispersion of a data set and is defined as the difference between the first quartile (Q1) and the third quartile (Q3) divided by 2.
 
• In this case, the first quartile (Q1) is 7.5. To find the third quartile (Q3), we first sort the data set in ascending order: 7, 8, 8, 9, 10.
 
• The third quartile (Q3) is the median of the upper half of the data set, so Q3 = 9. The quartile deviation is then calculated as (9 - 7.5) / 2 = 1.0.
